content.text:
I've submitted **index 0 (Sb fraction 0.22)** as the best composition. It gave the highest EQE I measured, 0.343%.

I used all 5 EQE measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.220 | **0.343** |
| 1 | 0.236 | 0.287 |
| 2 | 0.259 | 0.280 |
| 8 | 0.417 | 0.093 |
| 15 | 0.654 | 0.031 |

EQE drops steadily as the Sb fraction rises, so the best composition is at the zinc-rich end of the line. Index 0 matches the Zn₇Sb₂O₁₂ phase (Sb fraction 0.222). Near the ZnSb₂O₆ phase (Sb fraction 0.667), EQE was almost zero (0.031% at index 15).

**Limitations:**
- **High-Sb end not measured:** I didn't measure anything above Sb fraction 0.654. I skipped Sb 0.7–0.81 because the trend was clearly falling, but that is an inference, not a measurement.
- **Line edge:** index 0 is the first composition on the line. If the true peak is at even lower Sb, it isn't on this library.
- **No XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase assignments come from matching compositions to known phases, not from diffraction data.
- **Band-gap model:** the model predicted gaps of about 1.95 eV for both phases. I think that is too low. ZnSb₂O₆'s real gap is about 3.4 eV (from what I know, not from any tool), above the 3.2 eV light, which would explain its low EQE.
